results.caption_gt: Histopathology by H&E stain showing involvement of the dermis predominantly by spindle-shaped Schwannian cells and small nests of round melanocytes at 40X magnification. The histopathological examination revealed extensive involvement of the dermis by small nests of spindle-shaped melanocytes. Increased vascularity was noted, along with clusters of small, round melanocytes interspersed between collagen bundles and around epithelial adnexal structures, extending into the subcutaneous septa and between adipocytes. Rare pagetoid arrays of melanocytes were also observed as both single cells and round nests, with pale, vacuolated cytoplasm and dusty melanin. These findings were interpreted as NCH (Nodular Cellular Nevus) with Schwannian differentiation and focal mild atypical features within a CMN (Congenital Melanocytic Nevus), highlighting the complexity of this lesion.

results.caption_gt: Photomicrograph of a Spitz nevus harboring ALK fusion, showing a large, exophytic and dermal melanocytic proliferation with an infiltrative base. Clinically, ALK-fused Spitz neoplasms tend to be large and solitary papules or nodules, often arising on the extremities of young patients. Histologically, most of these lesions share a distinctive pattern substantiated by a compound wedge shape silhouette with a bulbous and/or infiltrative base. The proliferation is composed of nonpigmented, large, epithelioid and spindle melanocytes with amphophilic cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli, arranged in plexiform intersecting fascicles. H&E staining; original magnification 10×.

results.caption_gt: Photomicrograph showing a prototypical Spitz nevus, a benign melanocytic proliferation. This low-magnification view (original magnification 10×) highlights the distinctive architectural features of the lesion, which is symmetric, slightly raised, and compound, demonstrating a maturating melanocytic proliferation with epidermal hyperplasia and a flat base. The lesion often presents with a dome-shaped, wedge-shaped, or plaque-like silhouette, characterized by sharp lateral borders and maturation towards the deep part. Scattered Kamino bodies, which are small to large dull eosinophilic globules composed of amorphous filaments, may be seen. The pattern of growth is predominantly nested, composed of spindle and epithelioid melanocytes. The image is stained with Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E).

results.caption_gt: Photomicrograph illustrating a prototypical Spitz nevus, a benign melanocytic proliferation. This view (original magnification 100×) shows the characteristic architectural and cytological features, including large clefting nests of spindle and epithelioid melanocytes with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm. The lesion exhibits epidermal hyperplasia, and the overlying epidermis may be separated from the junctional nests and single melanocytes by clefts. Nests often display varying cellularity, size, and shape, and are typically arranged in parallel to the rete ridges. Scattered Kamino bodies, which are dull eosinophilic globules composed of amorphous filaments, are also present. The melanocytes feature moderately pleomorphic vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli. There is a predominance of enlarged epithelioid and/or spindle melanocytes with abundant eosinophilic or amphophilic cytoplasm, often with a “ground-glass” appearance, and round to oval to spindle nuclei with finely dispersed chromatin and distinct nucleoli. The image is stained with Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E).
